title: Review shared core primitives and root-level contracts in src/shared
scope: Primary ownership for root-level src/shared helpers and root contracts assigned to #410 in the shared-module ledger.

summary.overallAssessment: The root shared surface is mostly useful, but it is carrying too many neighboring responsibilities in a few high-consumer files. The main cleanup opportunities are in env/runtime policy composition, numeric normalization overlap, observability versus metrics versus ops helpers, and a few domain-specific contracts that do not belong in the root shared bucket.

clusterFindings.assessment: This is the weakest root-level cluster. env.js mixes runtime, bench, TUI, and test-only parsing; runtime-envelope.js re-parses overlapping env/runtime concerns; auto-policy.js bundles repo scanning, memoization, and runtime policy derivation; and toolchain/env path helpers live nearby without one obvious ownership story.

These helpers are individually useful, but limits.js and number-coerce.js overlap enough to create duplicate entry points for the same coercion decisions. sort.js and order.js are fine together, but their boundary should stay explicit. path-normalize.js is coherent and should remain the canonical repo-relative and platform path layer.

metrics.js and observability.js have a healthy conceptual split, but metrics.js has grown too wide. The ops-* helpers are useful but look like an undeclared family; their root-level placement hides that they are a coordinated operational diagnostics surface.

These are stable contracts, but both are specialized enough that root shared placement obscures ownership. The editor config contract is especially domain-specific and should not live in a miscellaneous root bucket.

highestPriorityFollowUps.reason: The file is the de facto env registry for runtime, testing, bench, extractor stubs, TUI, and misc feature flags. Its size and consumer count make boundary drift likely.
The file mixes environment patching, CLI/env/config precedence, NODE_OPTIONS parsing, and thread/runtime resolution. It should keep a facade but shed parsing and policy submodules.
Repo scanning and memoization are distinct concerns from quality/concurrency policy derivation and huge-repo preset selection.
A single file currently owns registry initialization plus many unrelated metric families. It should be decomposed by concern while preserving one shared registry.
Its API surface overlaps heavily with number-coerce.js. One module should become the canonical numeric-normalization entry point.
This is an editor integration contract and should live with contracts or editor integrations instead of the generic root shared bucket.

entries.consumerNotes: Consumed by indexing runtime bootstrap, build-index integration, and tooling config resolution; this is startup policy code rather than a narrow utility.
entries.recommendation: Keep buildAutoPolicy as the public facade, but split repo scanning/memoization, host sizing, and huge-repo preset selection into dedicated submodules.

entries.consumerNotes: Used mainly by runtime configuration assembly and a few build-time filters as a plain-object and recursive-merge utility.
entries.recommendation: Keep this module tiny and focused on config-shape primitives; do not let it absorb generic merge or coercion helpers.

entries.consumerNotes: Artifact writers and index-space checks use this for free-space enforcement and size estimation before expensive writes.
entries.recommendation: Keep the module, but document that it is the canonical disk-capacity helper and avoid duplicating byte-formatting and size-estimation logic elsewhere.

entries.consumerNotes: This is a stable cross-editor contract, but it is not a generic shared primitive and therefore has no direct runtime import consumers in the ledger.
entries.recommendation: Move this under a contracts or editor-integrations contract directory, then document it as the authoritative editor settings contract.

entries.consumerNotes: Command resolution and tooling install flows rely on it for PATH key normalization and de-duplication across Windows and POSIX environments.
entries.recommendation: Keep it separate from generic path normalization, but document the boundary against path-normalize.js and toolchain-env.js.

entries.consumerNotes: This is one of the highest-consumer shared modules in the repo, spanning CLI, indexing, retrieval, bench, TUI, test stubs, and provider/runtime behavior.
entries.recommendation: Split into focused surfaces such as runtime env, testing env, bench env, and feature-specific env helpers while keeping one stable public import surface if needed.

entries.consumerNotes: CLI, API, context-pack, diffs, and other surfaces consume it as the canonical error-code registry and payload builder.
entries.recommendation: Keep the error code registry centralized, but split heuristic hint resolution from the canonical code constants and payload builder so machine contracts stay clean.

entries.consumerNotes: Identity reconciliation, symbol handling, and a few language-provider paths depend on this for chunk and symbol envelopes.
entries.recommendation: Keep the module, but document the intended boundary between chunk identity, symbol identity, and artifact-row normalization to avoid ad hoc helpers elsewhere.

entries.consumerNotes: Validation, artifact helpers, and ordering checks use it for deterministic hashing and invariant enforcement.
entries.recommendation: Keep it small; if more invariant types accumulate, split deterministic hashing from assertion helpers rather than widening the bucket indefinitely.

entries.consumerNotes: Graph, contracts, indexing, and retrieval code use these list-normalization helpers broadly as low-level input coercion.
entries.recommendation: Keep this as the canonical iterable-to-array normalization surface and avoid adding unrelated collection transforms.

entries.consumerNotes: LSP, MCP, CLI display, and MCP transport flows use it for framed parsing and serialized JSON-RPC writing.
entries.recommendation: Keep the writer/parser pairing together, but document that this module owns framing and closed-stream handling, not higher-level protocol semantics.

entries.consumerNotes: Context-pack, graph, retrieval, and several budget/cap surfaces import this as one of the main numeric normalization entry points.
entries.recommendation: Collapse this surface into number-coerce.js or re-export from there so the repo has one obvious home for cap, limit, depth, and numeric coercion behavior.

entries.consumerNotes: Chunking, file processing, and tree-sitter execution use it for line-index and offset conversion logic.
entries.recommendation: Keep it as a narrow text-offset primitive module and resist adding broader text-processing helpers.

entries.consumerNotes: SCM, embeddings, LanceDB, and JSON-stream runtime paths use it to suppress duplicate warnings without central logger coupling.
entries.recommendation: Keep it focused on warn-once semantics and document it as the preferred duplicate-warning suppressor.

entries.consumerNotes: Artifact writers, graph-relations assembly, and validation paths use it as the repo's external-run merge and JSONL merge toolkit.
entries.recommendation: Split heap/planner primitives from JSONL run manifest and file-writing behavior so merge mechanics are reusable without dragging file-format concerns with them.

entries.consumerNotes: Watch, worker-pool, build-index integration, and risk/context-pack metrics all share this single prom-client registry module.
entries.recommendation: Preserve one registry, but split metric families into smaller files such as watch, worker, cache, fallback, and risk-pack metrics to make ownership explicit.

entries.consumerNotes: Capabilities and native-build tooling use it as the current no-go native-acceleration contract surface.
entries.recommendation: Keep the deterministic contract, but document that this is a feasibility and ABI decision module rather than a general runtime helper.

entries.consumerNotes: Artifact write control, pipeline checkpoints, and several concurrency/runtime paths already use this as a canonical numeric coercion helper.
entries.recommendation: Make this the primary numeric coercion surface and absorb or re-export overlapping limits.js helpers from here.

entries.consumerNotes: Core API, search, build-index integration, and router flows use it for correlation envelopes and observability propagation.
entries.recommendation: Keep this boundary distinct from metrics.js; it should continue to own correlation envelopes, context propagation, and transport headers.

entries.consumerNotes: Only a few orchestrator and search-plan paths consume it, and its behavior is explicitly test-config-driven rather than general runtime logic.
entries.recommendation: Move this into a declared ops or testing family so its test-oriented failure injection role is visible from the path alone.

entries.consumerNotes: Indexing and retrieval runners use it for stable preflight health-check records.
entries.recommendation: Keep the checks, but move it into an ops family alongside resource visibility so operational helpers stop living in a flat root bucket.

entries.consumerNotes: Indexing pipeline and retrieval telemetry use it for resource-growth thresholds and warning formatting.
entries.recommendation: Group this with ops-health and related operational diagnostics helpers under a dedicated ops family.

entries.consumerNotes: Compression, watchers, document extractors, and other optional-tool integrations rely on it for consistent dependency probing.
entries.recommendation: Keep it as the canonical optional dependency probe layer and document when callers should prefer tryRequire versus tryImport.

entries.consumerNotes: Artifact publication and repo-map style ordered outputs use it for stable ordering and deterministic ordering hashes.
entries.recommendation: Keep it as the higher-level ordering surface above sort.js, and document that compareStrings remains the low-level primitive comparator.

entries.consumerNotes: Context-pack, graph, incremental indexing, and repo-path handling use this heavily for repo-relative and platform-safe path normalization.
entries.recommendation: Keep it as the canonical repo/path normalization layer; document the boundary against env-path.js and files.js to prevent duplicate path helpers.

entries.consumerNotes: Indexer process-files, SCM snapshots, and tooling orchestrators use it to normalize and summarize reuse observations.
entries.recommendation: Keep it together as the reuse diagnostics surface, but document the distinction between observation normalization and summary aggregation.

entries.consumerNotes: Build runtime initialization, tree-sitter scheduler, dispatch env handling, and core build-index integration consume it for runtime resolution.
entries.recommendation: Retain one resolveRuntimeEnvelope facade, but split env-patch logic, node option parsing, and concurrency/runtime precedence resolution into dedicated internals.

entries.consumerNotes: Context-pack, graph, retrieval ranking, and many other surfaces use this as the default lexical comparator.
entries.recommendation: Keep it intentionally tiny as the primitive comparator and do not let it turn into a broader sorting utility bucket.

entries.consumerNotes: Bench and service progress-monitor surfaces use it for compact duration text rendering.
entries.recommendation: Keep it as a tiny display helper unless more time-format variants accumulate, in which case create a dedicated formatting family.

entries.consumerNotes: LSP client/provider startup and benchmark run loops use it to enforce Gradle daemon-off defaults.
entries.recommendation: Keep it small and explicit; document it as a toolchain-specific environment patch helper rather than a generic env utility.
